text:
sana_ml: flagging a weird quality regression on niseko-v2 int4 bring-up. repro on staging for zh/ja/zhuyin + ar. samples attached. :thinking_face:

hiro: saw the eval email. brief numbers?

sana_ml: quick summary: fp16 zh->ja BLEU=30.1, int4 BLEU=24.0 (delta -6.1). ja->en BLEU drop ~5.2. bopomofo tone marks and furigana (ruby) markers are disappearing in many decodes. ar->en shows missing tashkeel in outputs sometimes rearranged.

marco_infra: any tokenization diffs?

sana_ml: yes. examples: input (ja with ruby): "[漢字](かんじ)", expected tokens kept separate for ruby, but int4 tokenization yields merged token that removes the bracketed ruby. similar for bopomofo: tone diacritics collapsed into base.

kelsey_tokenizer: that's odd. int4 shouldn't modify tokenizer assets. can you paste the eval CLI?

sana_ml: here:
```
python tools/eval.py --model niseko-v2 --quant=int4 --splits=multi-locale --langs ja,zh,zh-bopo,ar,en --batch=256 --detokenize-check --out=tmp/niseko_int4.json
```

sana_ml: also ran a quick detok-roundtrip check; many inputs != detok(encode(detok)) on int4 nodes.

hiro: could the onboard packaging accidentally include a fallback detokenizer or alter the token map? we had a packaging tweak last week to speed up kernel lookup.

marco_infra: checking canary logs now.

marco_infra: log snippet:
```
[2026-05-01T14:05:02Z] kernel-selector: quant_kernel=int4_v3 requested
[2026-05-01T14:05:02Z] kernel-selector: compatibility check failed -> loading token_bin_compat_v1
[2026-05-01T14:05:03Z] tokenizer: loaded /opt/token_tables/token_bin_compat_v1.tbl
```

kelsey_tokenizer: token_bin_compat_v1 is a legacy table with limited unicode normalization for ruby/bopomofo/tashkeel. that explains the loss. how did nodes end up with that table?

marco_infra: packaging manifest shows artifact token_tables bundled changed from token_table_v2.tbl -> token_bin_compat_v1.tbl in release-niseko-v2-int4 wheel. blame: release script picks a compatibility artifact when kernel compatibility flag flips.

hiro: so kernel selector incompatibility caused fallback not only for kernel but also swapped token table for compatibility. that cascade is dangerous.

eval-bot: automated triage: signature matches mixedscript-detok-loss pattern, similarity=0.79 to prior ruby-loss cases. severity=P2.

taylor_prod: blocking release until fix. product notified. losing ruby/furigana can break downstream UX for customers in education vertical.

kelsey_tokenizer: immediate mitigation: we can publish a small compatibility shim that maps ruby/brackets back post-tokenize, but prefer to restore correct token_table_v2.tbl on int4 nodes.

hiro: plan: 1) revert packaging change so int4 wheel includes token_table_v2.tbl. 2) add a unit detok roundtrip test for ja/zh-bopo/ar in CI. 3) update kernel-selector to avoid switching token tables on fallback. 4) run int8/q5 runs to check sensitivity.

marco_infra: rolling a canary with token_table_v2.tbl now. starting eval re-run.

sana_ml: I ran a quick cpu-fallback reproduce (export USE_SOFT_KERNEL=1) and int4 CPU fallback yields BLEU=29.2 (almost baseline) and tokens look correct -> confirms runtime asset swap on GPU nodes.

marco_infra: canary re-run results: int4 w/ restored table BLEU=29.6 (delta -0.5). furigana and bopomofo preserved. tashkeel preserved.

kelsey_tokenizer: opened PR to change packaging: require explicit token_table pin in wheel metadata and add CI gate that rejects wheels that bundle token_bin_compat variants. cc @infra.

hiro: i'll file a follow-up to harden kernel-selector so token assets never change on fallback. assigning to @marco_infra.

taylor_prod: thanks. I'll update release plan: unblocking tentative after 24h of canary stability and full multi-split evals.

sana_ml: adding sample failures and the detok roundtrip test to the ticket. leaving int4 release on hold. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
